page.mentor_intro: Paget disease of bone is monitored with alkaline phosphatase and treated with potent intravenous bisphosphonates such as zoledronate, which give prolonged biochemical remission; some experts now suggest treating most patients at diagnosis.

teaching_points.claim: An Italian position paper notes the safety and long-term efficacy of zoledronate and suggests treating most, if not all, cases at diagnosis.
A clinical practice guideline says biochemical markers rather than symptoms indicate relapse, with assessment every 1 to 2 years after zoledronate and every 6 to 12 months with less potent drugs.
The 2019 JBMR guideline identified a lack of research on patient-focused clinical outcomes in Paget disease and several areas for future research.

In a Cochrane review of bisphosphonates in adults, mild gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 64% of treated and 48% of control participants (RR 1.32), with uncertain results for treatment discontinuation.
Epigenetic factors contribute to Paget disease pathogenesis and may provide diagnostic markers.

uncertainties: Whether treating asymptomatic disease prevents complications.

page.mentor_intro: Pancreatic cysts, most often IPMNs, are managed by risk stratification using worrisome features and high-risk stigmata. Many resections are for benign lesions, and small stable cysts may need less intensive surveillance.

page.mentor_intro: Pancreatogenic (type 3c) diabetes is accompanied by exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, which needs enzyme replacement titrated to nutritional status. Diagnostic testing for exocrine insufficiency remains limited in availability.

teaching_points.claim: The AGA update notes cross-sectional imaging cannot identify exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, and that breath tests and direct pancreatic function tests are promising but not widely available.

Pancreatic enzyme replacement dosing guidelines vary widely across disease types; most are initial doses, not upper limits, and doses should be titrated to nutritional status and response with regular follow-up.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency is common in coeliac disease, and is more frequent in patients with persistent symptoms on a gluten-free diet (28.4%) than in asymptomatic patients (3%).

Brazilian recommendations cover diagnosis and treatment of exocrine insufficiency including in pancreatic cancer patients, where enzyme replacement can improve symptoms, nutrition and quality of life.
Sarcopenia is common in chronic pancreatitis, and early detection and comprehensive care are advised.

page.mentor_intro: Pancytopenia work-up should consider marrow failure; for severe acquired aplastic anaemia current guidance adds eltrombopag to immunosuppression, requires expert-centre management and gives antimicrobial prophylaxis for neutropenia.

teaching_points.claim: The 2026 ASH guideline for severe and very severe aplastic anaemia recommends adding eltrombopag to immunosuppressive regimens and antibiotic and antifungal prophylaxis for patients with neutropenia, and describes a second-line option after failure of immunosuppression.

In children with severe aplastic anaemia, a systematic review supports adding eltrombopag to first-line immunosuppressive therapy; AIEOP guidelines cover acquired aplastic anaemia in childhood.

Diagnostic evaluation of unexplained pancytopenia mandates a systematic approach beginning with peripheral blood smear examination (evaluating for blasts, dysplastic neutrophils, teardrop cells, or hypersegmented neutrophils), nutritional assays (vitamin B12, folate), viral serologies (HIV, hepatitis, EBV, CMV), and bone marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy with cytogenetic analysis to distinguish aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and acute leukemias.

page.mentor_intro: Papilloedema from raised intracranial pressure, commonly idiopathic intracranial hypertension, threatens vision. Treatment combines weight loss, acetazolamide, and surgical options for refractory or severe visual loss.

teaching_points.claim: Venous sinus stenting is a safe and effective option for IIH patients unresponsive to medical therapy or with significant visual symptoms, but long-term outcomes need study.
Transorbital ultrasonography shows increased optic nerve sheath diameter and optic disc elevation associated with IIH, allowing non-invasive detection of raised ICP.

A meta-analysis of topiramate versus acetazolamide in IIH noted topiramate's benefit on weight reduction and acetazolamide's ability to lower CSF pressure and improve vision, recommending combination treatment.
Optic nerve sheath fenestration to preserve vision in IIH is supported by updated meta-analysis but is limited by publication bias.
GLP-1 and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists are under study in IIH, with randomised trials needed.

uncertainties: Optimal surgical option for vision-threatening disease.

page.mentor_intro: Paracetamol poisoning is treated with prompt acetylcysteine, which prevents liver injury when started early. Two-bag regimens are effective with fewer anaphylactoid reactions, and consensus statements standardise assessment and triage.

teaching_points.claim: A US and Canada consensus statement gives evidence-based recommendations for management of acetaminophen poisoning, and a separate consensus guides out-of-hospital triage of paracetamol exposure.
Early N-acetylcysteine, with treatment from 8 to 24 hours after overdose, is important to prevent or minimise liver damage regardless of regimen or route.
A two-bag acetylcysteine regimen was safe and effective and significantly reduced non-allergic anaphylactoid reactions compared with a three-bag regimen (OR 0.24).
The paracetamol-aminotransferase multiplication product can be used more than 24 hours after overdose and in staggered ingestions, addressing limitations of the Rumack-Matthew nomogram.
There is insufficient evidence to recommend fomepizole or cimetidine as primary or adjunct therapy in severe paracetamol poisoning.

uncertainties: Treatment of late presentations and staggered overdoses.

page.mentor_intro: Most patients labelled penicillin-allergic are not allergic. Delabelling by direct oral challenge or structured testing is safe, can be done by non-allergists, and improves antibiotic choice.

teaching_points.claim: Penicillin allergy delabelling by non-allergists is efficacious and safe, with reported harm about 0%; the proportion delabelled rises with complexity of testing, but many can be delabelled without skin testing.
Reactions to direct penicillin challenges are infrequent and comparable to indirect challenges after allergy testing, so direct challenge is safe across age groups and settings.
BSACI guidance supports delabelling services run by non-allergists for low-risk patients, with a framework for drug provocation testing and separate adult and paediatric sections.

Hong Kong consensus supports testing by non-allergists, with low-risk cases managed at spoke clinics supported by an allergist-led hub, and removal of inaccurate labels after a negative provocation test with counselling.
Surgical patients with a penicillin allergy label can be assessed and tested by trained professionals meeting minimum safe-testing standards.
The reported global prevalence of penicillin allergy comes mainly from high-income countries and secondary care.

uncertainties: Data from low-income settings.

page.mentor_intro: Periodic paralysis includes hypokalaemic and hyperkalaemic channelopathies and thyrotoxic forms. Treatment is trigger avoidance, potassium modification, diuretics and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, with dichlorphenamide the best-supported drug.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis supports dichlorphenamide in periodic paralysis with high-certainty evidence for primary outcomes and consistent efficacy across aetiologies and ages, although side effects need monitoring and counselling.
Treatment of periodic paralysis includes behavioural avoidance of triggers, modification of potassium levels, diuretics and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
A systematic review of hypokalaemic periodic paralysis case reports found phenotypic differences linked to different mutations and a suboptimal response to common preventive treatment.
A genome-wide meta-analysis found susceptibility loci for thyrotoxic periodic paralysis, including variants near genes implicated in monogenic muscle paralysis (KCNJ2, TRIM2).
Mutation-specific alterations in NaV1.4 function explain the diverse phenotypes of skeletal muscle sodium channelopathies.

teaching_points.claim: POISE: extended-release metoprolol started before non-cardiac surgery reduced a cardiac outcome (HR 0.73) but increased deaths (3.1% vs 2.3%) and strokes (1.0% vs 0.5%).

After cardiac surgery, perioperative beta-blockers prevent postoperative atrial fibrillation but did not translate into improved clinical outcomes.
In CABG, nearly all patients without contraindications are candidates for perioperative beta-blocker therapy, with carvedilol the most beneficial in one review.
Observational data suggest beta-blocker exposure relates to 30-day all-cause mortality but not to 30-day MACE or stroke, and commentary highlights potential harm of perioperative withdrawal.

uncertainties: Optimal handling in patients with established beta-blockade.

page.mentor_intro: Patients on long-term supraphysiological glucocorticoids or with confirmed primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency are at high risk of perioperative adrenal crisis due to suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis during surgical stress. Evidence-based guidelines stratify stress-dose hydrocortisone cover by procedural magnitude, balancing hemodynamics against infection and hyperglycemic risks.

teaching_points.claim: Patients receiving supraphysiological glucocorticoids (prednisolone >=5 mg/day or equivalent for >3-4 weeks) within the preceding 6-12 months are considered at risk of HPA axis suppression and require structured perioperative management.
For minor procedures under local anesthesia or conscious sedation, patients should take their usual morning oral glucocorticoid dose without supplemental parenteral hydrocortisone.

For major surgical procedures under general anesthesia, intravenous hydrocortisone (100 mg at induction, followed by 200 mg/24h continuous infusion or 50 mg IV every 6 hours) is maintained until oral intake and baseline oral maintenance dosing resume.

Acute perioperative adrenal crisis manifests with unexplained hypotension refractory to fluids and vasopressors, requiring immediate bolus intravenous hydrocortisone (100 mg) and isotonic saline resuscitation.

page.mentor_intro: Peripartum cardiomyopathy is managed with standard heart failure therapy adapted for pregnancy and lactation, with bromocriptine as a possible adjunct that improves LV recovery but lacks proven mortality benefit. Subsequent pregnancy carries risk when LV dysfunction persists.

teaching_points.claim: Prolactin inhibition with bromocriptine added to standard therapy was associated with significant improvement in LVEF and greater odds of LV recovery, without significant reduction in all-cause mortality.
A separate meta-analysis found bromocriptine associated with higher survival and LVEF improvement but not with fewer composite adverse clinical outcomes, and called for larger randomised trials.
In a subsequent pregnancy, persistent LV dysfunction beforehand carries higher mortality than recovered function, and subsequent pregnancy was associated with worsening echo parameters.
Contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI can serve as an adjunct to stratify the risk of poor LV recovery in postpartum PPCM if performed at a suitable time.
Receipt of guideline-directed medical therapy in PPCM differs by race and cardiology involvement, so additional equity strategies are needed.

uncertainties: Bromocriptine's role outside trials.

page.mentor_intro: PCOS management is metabolic and reproductive: lifestyle and metformin, with GLP-1 receptor agonists such as liraglutide adding benefit in overweight patients, and Italian guidance for infertility.

teaching_points.claim: Combined liraglutide and metformin in overweight or obese women with PCOS offered more comprehensive metabolic and hormonal benefits (including LH, FSH, testosterone and cholesterol) than metformin alone.
Liraglutide improved metabolic and reproductive outcomes in PCOS, though larger and longer trials are warranted to validate its reproductive efficacy and safety.
Continuing metformin after a positive pregnancy test seems to have greater clinical benefit than discontinuing it, but high-quality research is needed.
Italian guidelines adapt recommendations for diagnosis and management of infertility in PCOS, and the Society for Endocrinology guideline covers evaluation of androgen excess.
A global systematic review of PCOS prevalence informs international guideline diagnostic criteria and emphasises early, accurate diagnosis.

uncertainties: Long-term reproductive effects of GLP-1 treatment.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found cardiac amyloidosis is associated with increased mortality in severe aortic stenosis, and TAVR is safe and improves survival more than medical therapy or SAVR.
An HFA consensus statement covers management of aortic stenosis with chronic heart failure, focusing on pre- and post-procedural care in patients undergoing AVR.
In aortic stenosis with coronary disease, PCI+TAVR was associated with higher mortality or adverse events than CABG+SAVR, but lower perioperative complications.

In low and intermediate-risk patients, TAVR versus SAVR shows short-term benefits, but higher permanent pacemaker, paravalvular leak and reintervention rates raise concerns for younger, lower-risk patients.
Evidence does not support routine cerebral embolic protection during TAVR given no significant benefit in key outcomes.

page.mentor_intro: IPF carries high mortality: pooled 3-year survival is about 60-67%, and untreated mean overall survival is around 4 years. Antifibrotic therapy reduces all-cause mortality and acute exacerbation risk, and DLCO decline predicts death better than FVC in one registry.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found pooled 3-year cumulative survival of 59.9% before 2010 and 66.2% in the 2010s, noting no improving trend before 2010 and probable multifactorial improvement afterwards.
A systematic review of untreated IPF found pooled mortality of 12% at 1-2 years, 38% at 2-5 years and 69% at 5 years or more, with mean overall survival about 4 years.

A meta-analysis found antifibrotic treatment reduces all-cause mortality and the risk of acute exacerbation (pooled RR 0.63), with the acute exacerbation effect consistent for nintedanib but not pirfenidone.
Antifibrotic therapy protects against FVC decline in progressive pulmonary fibrosis, with similar efficacy for nintedanib and pirfenidone in IPF and non-IPF disease.

In an IPF registry, DLCO changes were a better predictor of mortality than FVC changes, and age 70 or above, high HRCT interstitial scores and DLCO fall of 15% or more at 12 months were adverse factors.
Real-world mortality and adverse events with pirfenidone and nintedanib were higher than in previous trials, with pirfenidone patients showing higher mortality.

uncertainties: Real-world safety differences between antifibrotics.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found the percentage of people developing reactive arthritis after Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella or Yersinia infection is relatively low (2.6%).

The BASHH national guideline gives management of sexually acquired reactive arthritis within UK sexual health services.
Updated estimates of sequelae after Campylobacter infection were provided, including for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis for the first time, with broad uncertainty.

A systematic review of intravesical BCG found autoimmune disorders, including articular and ocular groups, as complications.
